findings.excerpt: (x : R.Raw T) : R.map f (Quot.mk _ x) = Quot.mk _ (R.mapRing f x) := rfl
findings.problem: `map_mk` and `jOf_mk` are the computation rules for the quotient-defined `R.map` and `R.jOf` on class representatives. Neither carries `@[simp]`. Both are used only through hand-written `rw [map_mk, R.mapRing_id]`, `rw [map_mk, map_mk, map_mk, R.mapRing_comp]` and `rw [map_mk, jOf_mk, jOf_mk]` in `toLevelModuliDatum`. Because `Pt` is `Quot`, `R.map f (Quot.mk _ x)` cannot be normalised by `simp` without them. Each rule is a one-way reduction to a constructor-headed form and cannot cycle: the LHS is a defined function applied to `Quot.mk`, and the RHS is `Quot.mk` or `jOfUnit` of the representative. The repo already tags the analogous rule `ModuliPoint.map_mk` with `@[simp]`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark both lemmas `@[simp]`. Then `simp [R.mapRing_id]` and `simp [R.mapRing_comp]` can replace the explicit rewrite sequences in `map_id` and `map_comp`. The statements can stay as they are, since they are already oriented toward the representative.
findings.benefit: Downstream users of `toLevelModuliDatum` and `R.Pt` can use `simp` to push `map` and `jOf` through `Quot.mk` classes. Proofs of the functor and jOf compatibility laws no longer need a hand-counted `rw [map_mk, map_mk, map_mk, …]`, which is brittle.

evidence.excerpt: @[simp] theorem ModuliPoint.map_mk (σ : L →+* L') (P : Gamma0Pair N L)
| mk x => rw [map_mk, map_mk, map_mk, R.mapRing_comp]
